question: Should webchat shortcut discovery be owned by existing command inventory/plugin metadata, by a new first-party shortcut config surface, or by a plugin-contributed Control UI panel/contribution-slot design?
rationale: Current main has adjacent command discovery and plugin tabs but not user-defined prompt snippets, and the proposed config/storage shape crosses OpenClaw's high bar for new config surfaces.

options.title: Extend command inventory
options.body: Use existing `commands.list`/plugin command metadata as the canonical source and add UI affordances only where that model cannot express prompt insertion.

options.title: Approve first-party shortcuts config
options.body: Add a documented schema, migration/doctor behavior, UI, and tests for a new shortcut config or storage surface.

options.title: Defer to plugin contribution surface
options.body: Keep core lean and define or use a plugin Control UI contribution path for shortcut panels if maintainers want this outside first-party webchat.

recommendation.title: Extend command inventory
recommendation.body: Use existing `commands.list`/plugin command metadata as the canonical source and add UI affordances only where that model cannot express prompt insertion.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent Control UI, chat composer, and plugin tab work makes this the best available owner signal for the product/API direction choice.
